references.text: The Lord's hand is mentioned as an expression of God's power and judgment over Egypt, the same expression used in 9:3.
The fulfillment of the plague described in verse 3, where all the Egyptians' livestock died.
The Lord's hand is again mentioned as an instrument for pestilence and plagues against Egypt.
Pestilence (דֶּבֶר) as God's judgment; the same Hebrew word is used for severe disease as punishment.
The Lord's hand that weighed down the Philistines, parallel to God's hand over the Egyptians.
The psalm describes how God delivered the Egyptians' livestock to hail and pestilence, a poetic retelling of the plagues.
Pestilence (דֶּבֶר) as God's judgment, where disease strikes both people and animals.
The pale horse brings death with pestilence (θάνατος), reminiscent of the fifth plague against Egypt.
Direct allusion: Zechariah uses Exodus' description of cattle pestilence as a model for a future judgment.
